Given:
- True length of line $AB$ ($TL$) $= 60\text{ mm}$
- Line is parallel to V.P. and $20\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P.
- End A is $10\text{ mm}$ above H.P.
- End B is $50\text{ mm}$ above H.P.

### **Calculations for Inclination with H.P. ($\theta$):**
Since the line is parallel to V.P., its front view shows the true length and true inclination with H.P. ($\theta$).
Difference in heights of ends $A$ and $B$ = $50 - 10 = 40\text{ mm}$.
$$\sin(\theta) = \frac{\text{Difference in height}}{\text{True Length}} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3}$$
$$\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 41.81^\circ$$

### **Drawing Steps:**
1. Draw reference line $XY$.
2. **Top View:** Draw a line parallel to $XY$ at a distance of $20\text{ mm}$ below $XY$, representing the top view of length $60\text{ mm}$.
3. **Front View:** 
   - Mark end $a'$ at $10\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
   - Mark end $b'$ at $50\text{ mm}$ above $XY$, keeping the distance between their projectors equal to the horizontal length of the line.
   - Join $a'b'$ as a straight line of $60\text{ mm}$ true length.
4. Measure the angle made by $a'b'$ with the $XY$ line to graphically verify $\theta = 41.81^\circ$.
proTip: When a line is parallel to V.P., its front view gives the true length and true inclination with the H.P directly.
